To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
life satisfaction is a relatively stable cognitive construct that can be measured using social media data.

(a) life satisfaction posts on Twitter are not correlated to external events, (b) users who change their life satisfaction status over time are different in their psychosocial characteristics from users who do not change, and (c) users who change from life satisfaction to dissatisfaction post more negative affect and death related tweets than users who stay satisfied.
In summary, our research is concerned with
life satisfaction and the pursuit of happiness.
the study of the pursuit of happiness on Twitter.
the study of happiness and life satisfaction on social media.

life satisfaction and affect are two separate components of subjective well being and should be treated separately.
Twitter users who are satisfied with life are more positive and more optimistic than those who are dissatisfied.

life satisfaction is a somewhat stable cognitive construct that can be reliably detected in tweets.

life satisfaction can be measured on social media, and that it is possible to study trends in life satisfaction and its correlates over time.
